serialFormats.description: Rheem/Ruud HVAC (current style): 1 plant letter + WW (week) + YY (year) + 5-digit sequence, 10 characters total (e.g. W3520xxxxx = week 35 of 2020).

map.N: Fort Smith, AR (per building-center/pickhvac plant list)

sources: Building Intelligence Center — Rheem HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/rheem-hvac-age/): Style 1 = letter + 9 digits; first two digits after the letter = week, next two = year
PickHVAC — Rheem HVAC age / serial number decoding (https://www.pickhvac.com/hvac/age-serial-number/rheem/): M2215… = 22nd week of 2015; factory letter F, M, G, W or N
hvacchecker.com Rheem HVAC age: 10 characters = 1 factory letter, 4 date digits (WWYY), 5 sequence digits; W3520 = week 35 of 2020
Ruud HVAC age (https://www.building-center.org/ruud-hvac-age/): Ruud uses the same styles
notes: Week/year prefixes in the examples come from the cited decoders (W3520, M2215, 42/17); the 5-digit sequence portions are illustrative — the sequence does not affect the date.

Two-digit year with pivot 70: 95–99 → 1995–1999, 00–69 → 2000–2069. Serials in this style are common from the late 1990s on; a plate with an R-22 charge or a mid-1990s compressor date stamp with a yy of 95–99 is consistent with 199x.
Plant letter W appears on most current units; its plant is not documented in the cited sources (not mapped — do not guess).

Rheem's own page rheem.com/rheem_model_serial_numbers/ exists but its text could not be read in this session, so confidence stays 'medium' (two independent secondary decoders agree) rather than 'high'.
Ruud-branded units use the same serial styles (building-center Ruud page).

serialFormats.description: Rheem/Ruud HVAC older style: leading characters, then a mid-string plant letter (F, M, G, N or W) followed by WW (week) and YY (year) and a sequence (e.g. 5983 F 1096 12345 = week 10 of 1996).
sources: PickHVAC — Rheem HVAC age: 'the middle letter of the serial number is the factory code (F, M, G, W or N); week = 1st & 2nd numbers following it, year = 3rd & 4th' and 'Style 2: date coded in four numbers following the letter F, M, G or N (factory location)'
Building Intelligence Center — Rheem HVAC age: plant letters M = Montgomery AL, N = Fort Smith AR, F = Oxnard CA, G = Eagan MN
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE: the position/length of the characters preceding the plant letter could not be confirmed from a dated nameplate in this session; the regex tolerates 2–6 leading characters. The examples are synthetic (built from the published rule), not sourced nameplates — treat them as regex tests, not as dated evidence.

The rule itself (plant letter, then WW, then YY) is the same as the current style; the era filter (≤ 2005) is what separates this from 'rheem-hvac-letter-wwyy'. If both match, confirm the year from the compressor date code and the refrigerant on the plate (R-22 on pre-2010 units).
Oxnard CA and Eagan MN were closed long ago, so plant letters F and G on an HVAC plate point to an older unit.

sources: Building Intelligence Center — Rheem water heater age: Style 2 example 'RHLN 0106534307', week = 1st & 2nd digits, year = 3rd & 4th

controls.name: Rheem Renaissance Rooftop Unit Controller (RTU-C) with PlusOne Diagnostics / ClearControl
controls.description: Factory-mounted solid-state microprocessor rooftop unit controller on RKNL-C/RLNL-C and later Renaissance packaged units. Provides staging, economizer integration, diagnostics with alphanumeric fault codes on the local display and via ClearControl (DDL) / Modbus. The gas-heat IFC reports to the RTU-C over Modbus.

faultCodes.meaning: Controller fault — error with the control board itself.
likelyCauses: Controller internal fault / firmware error
Power-quality event (brown-out, transient) on the 24 VAC supply
Failed RTU-C board
checks: Cycle unit power off/on and see whether the code clears
Check 24 VAC control voltage at the controller under load (≥ 21 VAC) and the control transformer secondary fuse/breaker
If A15 returns after a power cycle with clean control power, replace the RTU-C board
faultCodes.source: Third-party service Q&A (justanswer: 'A15 controller fault — cycle power; if it persists the board must be replaced'); corroborated by parts-list description of the RTU-C as a solid-state controller
faultCodes.notes: Only code confirmed in this session. The full alphanumeric fault table is in the unit IOM (92-23577-80 series for RKNL-B/C) and the Renaissance Technology Guide — transcribe from there before relying on other codes.

diagnosticTips: Fault/status codes are shown on the controller display in the control compartment; PlusOne Diagnostics ('ClearControl') exposes the same data through the optional DDL/BAS interface (install instructions 92-103249-01).
The IFC (ignition control) on gas units communicates with the RTU-C via Modbus; an ignition fault will appear on the RTU-C display as well as on the IFC LED.
Clearing: most faults clear on power cycle; a lockout that returns immediately points to the safety that caused it (check HPS/LPS, limit, pressure switch history) rather than the board.

controls.name: Rheem/Ruud Integrated Furnace Control (IFC) LED flash codes — standard gas furnace / gas-pack ignition control
controls.description: Single-LED flash-code ignition control used across Rheem and Ruud gas furnaces and gas/electric packaged units (Rheem and Ruud share the platform, so codes are identical). The LED flashes a count, pauses, and repeats. On RKNL-C and later the IFC also reports the fault to the RTU-C via Modbus.

faultCodes.meaning: Pressure switch stuck open — the switch will not close when the inducer is on.
likelyCauses: Blocked or restricted flue/vent or combustion-air inlet
Condensate backed up into the pressure-switch hose (clogged drain/trap)
Inducer motor weak or not running
Cracked/loose pressure-switch tubing, failed pressure switch
checks: With the inducer running, measure draft at the switch tap with a manometer and compare with the switch's setpoint printed on it
Inspect and clear the condensate drain/trap and the switch tubing
Verify inducer runs at full speed and the vent is clear end to end
Jumper the switch only to prove the switch itself (never leave it jumpered)
faultCodes.source: Rheem 'Standard Gas Furnace Flash Codes' (pts.myrheem.com GF_Flash_Code) as summarized by multiple third-party guides (bcwide.ca, burkhardtheating.com, honestfix.com)

faultCodes.meaning: Limit switch open — main limit or roll-out (flame roll-out) control open.
likelyCauses: Low airflow: dirty filter, dirty evaporator coil, blower/belt problem, closed dampers, high external static
Blower not running / failed blower motor or capacitor
Roll-out switch tripped (blocked heat exchanger, flue restriction, burner misalignment) — manual-reset roll-out must be reset
Over-fired unit (gas pressure too high)
checks: Check whether a manual-reset roll-out switch is tripped before anything else
Measure temperature rise against the nameplate range and external static pressure
Verify blower operation in heat (speed/belt/motor amps)
Check manifold gas pressure and clocked input
faultCodes.source: Rheem 'Standard Gas Furnace Flash Codes' as summarized by multiple third-party guides (bcwide.ca, burkhardtheating.com, honestfix.com)

ledPatterns.pattern: Repeating group of N flashes, then pause
ledPatterns.meaning: Fault code N — count the flashes in one group
checks: Compare the count with the flash-code label on the control-box cover / IFC

diagnosticTips: The LED is on the IFC board in the burner/control compartment; the code legend is printed on the board label and the unit's flash-code label (e.g. 92-103343-01 for 2-digit-display furnaces).
A clogged condensate line that backs up into the pressure-switch hose is a common cause of a 2-flash fault on gas packs.
Clear a lockout by cycling thermostat demand (W off/on) or unit power; a roll-out switch is manual reset and must be pressed after the cause is fixed.

diagnosticTips: Display/LEDs: the module is in the economizer/control compartment; use the ▲/▼/Enter/Esc buttons to walk STATUS → SETPOINTS → SYSTEM SETUP → ADVANCED SETUP → CHECKOUT → ALARMS.
CHECKOUT drives the damper open/closed and exercises outputs for testing; STATUS shows live MAT/OAT/RAT, economizer availability and damper position.
Alarms clear automatically when the condition is resolved (e.g. a sensor reconnected); a persistent alarm after wiring is verified means the sensor or actuator is bad.

controls.name: AAON Orion (WattMaster) VCCX2 / VCC-X unit controller
controls.description: Factory-installed AAON unit controller (Orion Control Systems / WattMaster) on RN, RQ and other AAON rooftops. Alarms are text alarms shown on the LCD / System Manager TS-L/TS II and via BACnet; the red ALARM LED lights continuously while any alarm is present. Companion modules: RSMD/RSMD2R refrigerant system module, CPM compressor protection module, head-pressure control module. Coverage is partial: the VCCX2 technical guide's alarm sections (p.89-92) were transcribed from search-result excerpts, not read in full; exact trigger text for Mechanical Cooling Failure and Mechanical Heating Failure, and full definitions for the Title 24 'Not Economizing When It Should' / 'Economizing But Shouldn't', Relay Run Time Exceeded, Fan Array Controller and Direct Fire Heat alarms were not captured (names confirmed in the guide's alarm list). A 'High Control Temp Failure Alarm' likely exists (the guide defines a 'Control Mode High Alarm Offset' used when the controlling sensor rises above the Cooling Mode Enable Setpoint) but the alarm name was not seen verbatim, so it is not included. The 6 codes in the existing pack entry are all retained here (Low Suction Pressure Failure, Mechanical Cooling Failure, Mechanical Heating Failure, Fan Proving Alarm, Dirty Filter Alarm, sensor failure alarms - the last now split into Bad SAT / OAT / Space / RAT / CO2 sensor entries). Meanings were tightened to the guide text where search excerpts allowed. VCCX-IP (ASM07424) and VCCX-454 (ASM07503, R-454B u

faultCodes.meaning: Suction pressure stays below the Low Suction Pressure Setpoint for one minute or falls below 40 psi for five seconds; the system shuts down and power must be cycled to clear the alarm.
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge / leak
Low evaporator airflow (dirty filters, VFD/fan fault, iced coil)
Restricted TXV/EEV or liquid line
Failed suction pressure transducer or wiring
checks: Verify suction transducer reading against a gauge on the same port
Check charge by subcooling with the compressor forced to full capacity
Check airflow: filters, fan speed command vs actual, coil condition
Inspect for frost at the metering device (restriction)
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide (G039840, software SS1088), alarm description

faultCodes.meaning: Listed in the VCCX2 technical guide under 'Mechanical Failure and Failure Mode Alarms' (LCD alarm text 'MECH COOL FAIL' on the Orion controller family): the controller detected that mechanical cooling did not produce the expected supply-air result while in Cooling Mode. The exact trigger delay/offset text was not captured in search summaries.
likelyCauses: Compressor(s) not running: RSMD compressor fault or lockout, CPM/compressor-controller trip, contactor, overload, high/low pressure switch
Refrigerant circuit fault (low charge, restriction, failed EEV/digital scroll unloader)
Supply air temperature sensor reading wrong so cooling proof is never seen
Condenser fan / head-pressure control failure
checks: Read the RSMD/RSMD2R module alarm screen and the compressor controller ALERT/TRIP LEDs before condemning the VCCX2
Confirm cooling stage relay LEDs (RLY) are on and 24 VAC reaches the compressor contactor coil
Verify supply air temperature sensor against a reference thermometer in the supply duct
Check charge by subcooling with the digital scroll forced to 100 percent
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Mechanical Failure and Failure Mode Alarms' (ManualsLib p.91); Orion System Manager TS II manual module alarm list ('MECH COOL FAIL')

faultCodes.meaning: Listed in the VCCX2 technical guide under 'Mechanical Failure and Failure Mode Alarms': heating was called while in Heating Mode but the supply air did not respond as expected. Note mechanical heating is disabled when the Outdoor Air Temperature is above the Heating Lockout Setpoint. Exact trigger text not captured in search summaries.
likelyCauses: Gas heat ignition control lockout (check the furnace's own ignition-control LED)
Electric heat: open limit, failed contactor/SCR, blown heater fuse
Hot water/steam: valve or pump failure
Supply air temperature sensor fault
checks: Confirm heat stage relay LEDs are on and the heat section's own diagnostics (ignition control / limit) are clear
Verify supply air temperature rise with heat energized
Verify OAT is below the Heating Lockout Setpoint (heat will not run above it)
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Mechanical Failure and Failure Mode Alarms' (ManualsLib p.91) and Heating Mode sequence (p.71)

faultCodes.meaning: Supply fan proving input did not close after the fan was commanded on.
likelyCauses: Supply fan/VFD not running (VFD fault, belt, overload)
Proving switch (differential pressure or current sensor) failed or mis-set
Wiring open to the proving input
checks: Check VFD status/fault log and fan rotation
Verify the proving switch closes with the fan running (24 VAC at the input)
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide (G039840), alarm list

faultCodes.meaning: Dirty filter status — a differential pressure switch provides a 24 VAC wet-contact closure to indicate a dirty filter.
likelyCauses: Loaded filters
Filter switch set too low or tubing reversed
checks: Inspect filters; verify switch setpoint and tubing (high side upstream of the filters)
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide (G039840), input description

faultCodes.code: Sensor failure alarms (space, supply, outdoor, return, etc.)
faultCodes.meaning: Alarm generated when a configured temperature/humidity/pressure sensor reads open or shorted (see 'Alarm Detection and Sensor Failure Alarms' section).
likelyCauses: Open/shorted 10k Type III thermistor or wiring
Sensor not installed but configured
checks: Measure sensor resistance at the controller input
Check configuration for sensors that are not actually installed
faultCodes.source: AAON Orion VCCX2 Technical Manual, section 'Alarm Detection and Sensor Failure Alarms' (ManualsLib p.89)

faultCodes.meaning: 'Failure Proof of Flow Interlock Alarm' on the LCD alarm screen ('FAN POF'). The Fan Proving input (BI1 'Proof of Airflow', 24 VAC wet contact) is required to protect the equipment from running without the main fan being on; if the proof of flow contact does not close after the supply fan is commanded on, the alarm is generated and the unit is prevented from running heating/cooling.
likelyCauses: Supply fan / VFD not running (VFD fault, broken belt, overload, disconnect open)
Proving device (differential pressure switch or current switch) failed, mis-set, or tubing plugged
Open wiring or missing 24 VAC to BI1 (dry contacts are not recognized - the input needs 24 VAC)
checks: Check the VFD keypad/fault log and fan rotation
With the fan running, measure 24 VAC at BI1; if absent, jumper the proving switch to isolate switch vs wiring
Verify the proving switch setpoint and tubing orientation
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, Binary Inputs (BI1 Proof of Airflow) and 'Alarm Screens' (ManualsLib 2236153 p.112: 'FAN POF')

faultCodes.meaning: Exhaust Fan / Return Fan Proof of Flow alarm: added as BI:126 'Exhaust Fan / Return Fan Proof of Flow Alarm' in later SS1088 revisions; generated when the return/exhaust fan proof-of-flow input does not prove after the fan is commanded on.
likelyCauses: Return/exhaust fan or its VFD not running
Proving switch failed or not wired to the configured expansion input
Input not configured to match the installed proving device
checks: Verify the fan is actually running and the proving contact closes (24 VAC at the input)
Check the binary input configuration in Prism 2 / service tool matches the installed hardware
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, revision history (BI:126 Exhaust Fan / Return Fan Proof of Flow Alarm) and 'Mechanical Failure and Failure Mode Alarms'

faultCodes.meaning: A differential pressure switch is used to provide a 24 VAC wet contact closure (BI2) to indicate a Dirty Filter status; the closure generates the Dirty Filter Alarm (LCD text 'DIRTY FILTER').
likelyCauses: Filters loaded
Filter switch setpoint too low, tubing reversed or plugged
Switch wired to the wrong input
checks: Inspect/replace filters; the alarm should clear once the switch opens
Verify the switch setpoint and that the high-pressure tap is upstream of the filters
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, Binary Inputs (BI2 Dirty Filter) and 'Alarm Screens' (ManualsLib 2236153 p.112)

faultCodes.meaning: BI8 Emergency Shutdown Input is a 24 VAC wet contact input used to initiate shutdown of the HVAC unit when a normally closed smoke detector, firestat, or other shutdown condition contact is opened. If the contact opens, it will initiate shutdown of the VCCX2 and will generate an alarm condition; the unit immediately removes all compressor and heating outputs. If an Occupied relay is configured, it will remain energized; the controller stays active and can still drive alarm relays.
likelyCauses: Smoke detector, firestat, or other life-safety contact tripped
Loss of 24 VAC to the shutdown loop (blown fuse, loose wire, tripped phase monitor feeding the loop)
Smoke detector needs reset after a test or dust event
checks: Check the smoke detector / firestat status and reset it
Measure 24 VAC at BI8 with the loop intact; trace the loop for an open contact or broken wire
Do not jumper the input except momentarily for diagnosis - it is a life-safety interlock
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, Binary Inputs (BI8 Emergency Shutdown) and 'Mechanical Failure and Failure Mode Alarms' (ManualsLib p.91); 'Alarm Screens' p.112 ('EMERG SHUTDOWN')

faultCodes.code: Bad SAT Sensor (Supply Air Temperature Sensor Failure)
faultCodes.meaning: The Supply Air Temperature Sensor Failure Alarm is generated when the controller detects an open or short circuit on the Supply Air Temperature input. The controller continuously performs self diagnostics during normal operation to determine if any operating failures have occurred. Sensor diagnostics: a voltage above 4.88 VDC at the input indicates an open sensor or wiring; less than 0.05 VDC indicates a short.
likelyCauses: Open or shorted 10k Type III thermistor or its wiring
Sensor unplugged / connector corroded
Wrong sensor type installed
checks: Measure input voltage at the controller: >4.88 VDC = open, <0.05 VDC = short
Disconnect and measure sensor resistance (about 10k ohms at 77 F) and compare to the temperature/resistance table
Repair wiring or replace the sensor; the alarm clears when a valid reading returns
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Alarm Detection and Sensor Failure Alarms' (ManualsLib p.89) and Troubleshooting sensor voltage table

faultCodes.code: Bad OAT Sensor (Outdoor Air Temperature Sensor Failure)
faultCodes.meaning: Outdoor Air Temperature sensor reads open or shorted. Failsafe: when the Outdoor Air Temperature Sensor fails, the Outdoor Air reading will be artificially set to the half point between the Cooling and Heating Lockout Setpoints, which allows the cooling and heating to continue operating (economizer free cooling is lost).
likelyCauses: Open/shorted OAT thermistor or wiring (sensor is outdoors - UV/moisture damage common)
E-BUS outdoor temperature/humidity sensor not communicating
checks: Check voltage at the OAT input (>4.88 VDC open, <0.05 VDC short) or E-BUS sensor status
Measure sensor resistance at the controller end to include wiring
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Alarm Detection and Sensor Failure Alarms' (ManualsLib p.89) - OAT failsafe text

faultCodes.code: Bad Space Sensor (Space Temperature Sensor Failure)
faultCodes.meaning: Space temperature sensor reads open or shorted (same open/short detection as the other thermistor inputs). Listed among the VCCX2 alarms ('Bad Space Sensor').
likelyCauses: Open/shorted wall sensor or wiring
Sensor configured as the controlling sensor but not installed
E-BUS digital space sensor not communicating
checks: Check input voltage / resistance at the controller
If the unit is supposed to control from supply or return air, correct the configuration instead of adding a sensor
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Alarm Detection and Sensor Failure Alarms' (ManualsLib p.89)

faultCodes.code: Bad RAT Sensor (Return Air Temperature Sensor Failure)
faultCodes.meaning: Return air temperature sensor reads open or shorted. Listed among the VCCX2 alarms ('Bad RAT Sensor').
likelyCauses: Open/shorted return air thermistor or wiring
Sensor configured but not installed
checks: Check input voltage / resistance at the controller; verify configuration
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Alarm Detection and Sensor Failure Alarms' (ManualsLib p.89)

faultCodes.meaning: When the VCCX2 expects a CO2 sensor but does not detect it, IAQ Mode is disabled and the alarm is generated. If the sensor is properly detected after the unit has alarmed, the alarm will be cleared and the unit will return to CO2 control.
likelyCauses: E-BUS space or duct CO2 sensor unplugged / not communicating
Sensor configured but never installed
Sensor power or E-BUS cable fault
checks: Check the E-BUS cable and sensor power; watch the E-BUS LED for traffic
Confirm the CO2 configuration matches the installed sensor
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Alarm Detection and Sensor Failure Alarms' (ManualsLib p.89)

faultCodes.code: Airflow Sensor Alarm (Outdoor / Supply / Return Airflow Sensor Alarm)
faultCodes.meaning: If the controller is configured to have any airflow sensors, but the controller does not detect that the sensor is connected, then the applicable alarm (Outdoor Airflow Sensor Alarm, Supply Airflow Sensor Alarm, Return Airflow Sensor Alarm) will occur. If the sensor is properly detected after the unit has alarmed, the alarm will be cleared.
likelyCauses: EBTRON / GreenTrol / Paragon airflow station not communicating or unpowered
Airflow monitoring configured for an air stream that has no station
checks: Check station power and its E-BUS / signal wiring
Remove the airflow configuration for streams without a station
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Alarm Detection and Sensor Failure Alarms' - Airflow Alarms (ManualsLib p.89)

faultCodes.meaning: Temperature protection: if the supply air temperature drops below the Low Supply Air Temperature Cutoff Setpoint for 10 minutes, the Low Supply Air Temperature Cutoff Alarm is generated and cooling is cut off. This mode and alarm will be cancelled if the Supply Air Temperature rises above the Low Supply Air Temperature Cutoff Setpoint by 5 degrees.
likelyCauses: Low airflow across the evaporator (dirty filters, VFD too slow, iced coil)
Compressor not staging off / digital scroll stuck loaded
Cold outdoor air with economizer or damper stuck open in heating season
Supply air sensor reading low
checks: Compare SAT reading to a reference thermometer
Check filters, fan speed vs command, and coil for ice
Verify economizer damper position vs command
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, temperature protection / 'Mechanical Failure and Failure Mode Alarms' (ManualsLib p.91)

faultCodes.meaning: Temperature protection is activated immediately when the supply air temperature rises above the user-adjustable High Supply Air Temperature Cutoff Setpoint; heating is disabled and the High Supply Air Temperature Cutoff alarm is generated.
likelyCauses: Low airflow with heat energized (filters, fan speed, closed dampers)
Heat stage stuck on (welded contactor, gas valve not closing)
Cutoff setpoint set too low for the heat type
checks: Check airflow and that heat relays de-energize when commanded off
Verify the High SAT Cutoff Setpoint is appropriate
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, temperature protection / 'Mechanical Failure and Failure Mode Alarms' (ManualsLib p.91)

faultCodes.meaning: When the Space (controlling sensor) Temperature drops below the Heating Mode Enable Setpoint minus the Control Mode Low Alarm Offset setpoint for 30 seconds, the controller will generate a Low Control Temp Failure Alarm.
likelyCauses: Heating not keeping up (see Mechanical Heating Failure)
Unit off / unoccupied with low setback
Alarm offset set too tight
checks: Confirm heating is operating and staging
Review Heating Mode Enable Setpoint and Control Mode Low Alarm Offset
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Mechanical Failure and Failure Mode Alarms' (ManualsLib p.91)

faultCodes.code: Title 24 Economizer Air Temperature Sensor Failure
faultCodes.meaning: Title 24 (FDD) Economizer alarm: Economizer Temperature Sensor Failure occurs when the Outside Air or Supply Air Temperature Sensor is shorted or missing.
likelyCauses: Open/shorted OAT or SAT sensor or wiring
checks: Diagnose as for Bad OAT / Bad SAT Sensor
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Title 24 Economizer Alarms' (ManualsLib p.92)

faultCodes.meaning: Title 24 (FDD) Economizer alarm generated when the economizer is enabled but the damper feedback signal (0-10 VDC into the EM1 expansion module) is not within 10 percent of the desired position.
likelyCauses: Actuator failed, stripped, or lost power
Feedback wire open or not connected to the EM1
Damper linkage bound
checks: Command the damper from the service tool and compare the feedback voltage to the command
Verify actuator power and feedback wiring at the EM1
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Title 24 Economizer Alarms' (ManualsLib p.92)

faultCodes.meaning: Title 24 (FDD) Economizer alarm generated when the economizer is not enabled but the feedback signal indicates a damper position more open than the minimum position.
likelyCauses: Actuator not closing to minimum (failed spring return, wrong stroke)
Feedback signal offset / mis-scaled
BAS override holding the damper open
checks: Check the actual damper position against the minimum setpoint and the feedback voltage
Look for BACnet/BAS overrides on the economizer output
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Title 24 Economizer Alarms' (ManualsLib p.92)

faultCodes.code: Title 24 Economizer Not Economizing When It Should
faultCodes.meaning: Title 24 (FDD) Economizer alarm listed by name in the VCCX2 technical guide: conditions are suitable for economizer cooling but the economizer is not economizing. Detailed trigger text not captured in search summaries.
likelyCauses: Economizer disabled by configuration or enthalpy/dry-bulb changeover setpoints
Damper failed closed
OAT or OA humidity sensor reading incorrectly
checks: Verify economizer enable setpoints and the OAT / OA humidity readings
Command the damper open and confirm feedback
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Title 24 Economizer Alarms' (ManualsLib p.92) - alarm name

faultCodes.meaning: Title 24 (FDD) Economizer alarm listed by name in the VCCX2 technical guide: the economizer is economizing when outdoor conditions do not permit it. Detailed trigger text not captured in search summaries.
likelyCauses: Damper stuck open / actuator failed
Changeover setpoint mis-set
OAT sensor reading low
checks: Compare OAT reading and changeover setpoints; check damper position vs command
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, 'Title 24 Economizer Alarms' (ManualsLib p.92) - alarm name

faultCodes.meaning: Alarm listed by name in the VCCX2 technical guide alarm list ('relay run time exceeded alarm'): a relay output's accumulated run time has exceeded its configured run-time limit (maintenance reminder). Detailed text not captured in search summaries.
likelyCauses: Scheduled maintenance interval reached for the associated output (filters, belts, compressor hours)
checks: Perform the maintenance, then reset the run-time counter in Prism 2 / service tool
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, alarm list (relay run time exceeded alarm)

faultCodes.meaning: Alarm listed by name in the VCCX2 technical guide alarm list ('Fan Array Controller alarm'); the VCCX2 (SS1088 v2.36+) also exposes Fan Array Controller motor current and speed percent over BACnet. Detailed trigger text not captured in search summaries.
likelyCauses: Fan array (ECM/EC fan wall) controller reporting a motor fault or loss of communication
checks: Read the fan array controller's own status and each fan's fault LED; check its E-BUS/communication link to the VCCX2
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, alarm list; SS1088 VCCX2 revision log (v2.36 BACnet fan array points)

faultCodes.meaning: Alarm listed by name in the VCCX2 technical guide alarm list ('direct fire heat alarm') for units with a direct-fired gas heat section. Detailed trigger text not captured in search summaries.
likelyCauses: Direct-fired burner flame safeguard lockout or airflow proving fault
checks: Check the burner flame-safeguard control's own fault code and the burner airflow proving switch
faultCodes.source: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840, alarm list (direct fire heat alarm)

faultCodes.code: Low Suction Pressure Failure (RSMD: LOW SUCT / SP1)
faultCodes.meaning: RSMD refrigerant system module alarm: occurs if suction pressure stays below the Low Suction Pressure Setpoint for one minute or falls below 40 psi for five seconds. This alarm will shut down the system and power must be cycled to clear the alarm.
likelyCauses: Low refrigerant charge / leak
Low evaporator airflow (dirty filters, VFD/fan fault, iced coil, closed dampers)
Restricted TXV/EEV, liquid line drier, or plugged strainer
Failed suction pressure transducer or wiring reading low
checks: Verify the suction transducer against a gauge on the same port (the RSMD diagnostic screen shows the transducer reading)
Check charge by subcooling with the compressor forced to full capacity
Check airflow: filters, fan speed command vs actual, coil condition
Look for frost at the metering device (restriction); then cycle power to the RSMD to clear the lockout
faultCodes.source: RSMD Technical Guide G039810 / RSMD2R G088350, alarm definitions ('Low Suction Pressure'); AAON RSMD Technical Manual (ManualsLib) p.17 'Alarms Screen and Definitions'

faultCodes.meaning: RSMD-CM alarm for the second circuit: occurs if Suction Pressure 2 stays below the Low Suction Pressure Setpoint for one minute or falls below 40 psi for five seconds. This alarm will shut down the system and power must be cycled to clear the alarm. (One ManualsLib RSMD summary states a 20-second delay for SP2 - confirm against the module's own guide.)
likelyCauses: Same as circuit 1: low charge, low airflow, restriction, bad transducer on circuit 2
checks: Diagnose circuit 2 as for Low Suction Pressure Failure; cycle power to the RSMD to clear
faultCodes.source: RSMD-CM Technical Guide G102439 Rev. A / AAON RSMD-CM Technical Manual (ManualsLib) p.19 'Alarms Screens'

faultCodes.meaning: RSMD high head pressure alarm condition, activated when the head pressure (Head Pressure 1 or Head Pressure 2) rises above 550 psi; this causes the condenser output to go to 100 percent. Power must be cycled to the RSMD to clear the alarm. (RSMV variant: alarm deactivates when head pressure drops below 540 psig.)
likelyCauses: Condenser fan not running / head-pressure control output failure
Dirty or blocked condenser coil, recirculating hot air
Overcharge or non-condensables
Failed head pressure transducer reading high
checks: Verify the transducer against a gauge on the discharge/liquid line
Check condenser fan operation and the 0-10 VDC condenser signal
Clean the coil; check subcooling for overcharge; then cycle RSMD power to clear
faultCodes.source: RSMD Technical Guide G039810, alarm definitions ('High Head Pressure Detected'); RSMV Technical Guide AA-RSMV-TGD-D (540 psig release)

faultCodes.code: Suction Pressure Sensor Failure / No Suction Pressure Detected
faultCodes.meaning: RSMD alarm: indicates the Suction Pressure Sensor (transducer) is not detected by the system. There is no compressor failure from this alarm; the failure will be unsafe suction pressure (low-suction protection is lost). RSMD sensor diagnostics: voltage above 4.98 VDC indicates an open sensor or wiring; less than 0.38 VDC indicates a shorted sensor.
likelyCauses: Transducer unplugged, open/shorted cable, or failed transducer
Transducer not powered (5 VDC supply)
checks: Measure transducer signal voltage at the RSMD (>4.98 VDC open, <0.38 VDC short) and the 5 VDC supply
Compare the RSMD diagnostic-screen pressure to a gauge; replace the transducer if the signal is wrong
faultCodes.source: AAON RSMD Technical Manual (ManualsLib) p.17 'Alarms Screen and Definitions'; RSMD2R Technical Guide G088350 ('No Suction Pressure Detected'); RSMD guide sensor voltage diagnostics

faultCodes.code: Head Pressure Sensor Failure / No Head Pressure Detected
faultCodes.meaning: RSMD alarm: indicates the Head Pressure Sensor 1 (or 2) is not detected by the system. This will cause the condenser fan/valve output to go to 100 percent (loss of head pressure reading drives the condenser signal to 100 percent until the compressor shuts down).
likelyCauses: Transducer unplugged, open/shorted cable, or failed transducer
5 VDC transducer supply missing
checks: Measure transducer signal voltage (>4.98 VDC open, <0.38 VDC short) and supply at the RSMD
Expect the condenser fans at full speed while this alarm is active - do not chase that as a separate fault
faultCodes.source: AAON RSMD Technical Manual (ManualsLib) p.17 'Alarms Screen and Definitions'; RSMD2R G088350 ('No Head Pressure Detected'); RSMVHPQ Technical Guide ASM02786

faultCodes.meaning: RSMD alarm: occurs if the compressor fails to run 45 seconds after the relay is activated or if the run signal is lost after activation. Binary Input 1 is the Compressor 1 status, typically sourced from the auxiliary contacts on the compressor contactor after it has run through the compressor safeties; if it opens, the Compressor Enable Relay de-energizes and a compressor alarm is generated, with a retry after five minutes. If a COMP 1 or 2 fault occurs five times within a four-hour period, the compressor will be locked out and power must be cycled to the RSMD to clear the alarm.
likelyCauses: Compressor safety open in the contactor coil circuit (HPS, LPS, compressor controller TRIP, phase monitor)
Contactor not pulling in / bad aux contact or aux contact wiring
Compressor overload or internal protector open
Compressor controller (Copeland DCC) in alarm - read its flash code
checks: With the RSMD relay energized, check 24 VAC through the safety string to the contactor coil and note which device opened
Verify the aux contact closes and 24 VAC returns to the RSMD binary input
Read the compressor controller ALERT LED flash code
After repair, cycle power to the RSMD to clear a lockout
faultCodes.source: AAON RSMD Technical Manual (ManualsLib) p.17 'Alarms Screen and Definitions'; RSMD Technical Guide G039810 binary input description

faultCodes.code: Compressor 1 / 2 HPS Fault (RSMD-CM: COMP1 HPS FAULT)
faultCodes.meaning: RSMD-CM alarm: occurs if the compressor relay is energized and the binary input is energized but the binary input de-energizes within the first 15 minutes of the compressor call (high pressure switch trip). The module allows four retries but locks out on the fifth fault; the retry count resets if the RSMD-CM goes to Off Mode or the compressor has run successfully for two hours since the last fault.
likelyCauses: High pressure switch tripping: condenser fan/head-pressure control failure, dirty coil, overcharge, non-condensables
HPS wiring intermittent
checks: Watch head pressure on the RSMD diagnostic screen as the compressor starts
Verify condenser fan operation and coil cleanliness; check the HPS trip point
Cycle power to the RSMD-CM to clear the lockout after repair
faultCodes.source: RSMD-CM Technical Guide G102439 Rev. A / AAON RSMD-CM Technical Manual (ManualsLib) p.19 'Alarms Screens'

faultCodes.meaning: RSMD-CM alarm: indicates that communication has been lost between the RSMD-CM and the Main controller (VCCX2) or other E-BUS modules that may be connected.
likelyCauses: E-BUS cable unplugged or damaged
Module address/DIP switch conflict
Main controller halted or powered down
checks: Check E-BUS cables and connectors between the VCCX2 and modules; watch the COMM/EBUS LEDs for activity
Verify module addressing and that the VCCX2 heartbeat LEDs are blinking
faultCodes.source: RSMD-CM Technical Guide G102439 Rev. A / AAON RSMD-CM Technical Manual (ManualsLib) p.19 'Alarms Screens'

faultCodes.meaning: RSMD alarm: if the module's Emergency Shutdown binary input is activated, the RSMD generates an alarm and shuts down the compressor relay.
likelyCauses: Unit shutdown loop (smoke/firestat/phase monitor) open
Loss of 24 VAC to the shutdown input
checks: Check the shutdown loop and the VCCX2 Emergency Shutdown alarm (usually present together)
faultCodes.source: RSMD Technical Guide G039810, binary input / alarm description

faultCodes.code: Compressor controller ALERT Flash Code 2 - High Discharge Temperature
faultCodes.meaning: Copeland Digital Compressor Controller (used on AAON RN/RQ digital scroll compressors) ALERT flash code 2: discharge thermistor above trip set point or thermistor short circuited. Resets after 30 minutes and motor cools down; if 5 events occur within 4 hours, the compressor is locked out. Flash code 2 activates the 30-minute anti-short-cycle timer.
likelyCauses: Low charge / low suction density (high superheat) overheating the scroll
High compression ratio: dirty condenser, condenser fan failure
Digital scroll unloading with poor return gas cooling
Shorted discharge thermistor
checks: Measure discharge line temperature and suction superheat; check charge and condenser operation
Check thermistor resistance; replace if shorted
Cycle power after repair if locked out
faultCodes.source: AAON RN Series IOM, Table 33 'Compressor Controller ALERT Flash Codes' / Figure 'Compressor Controller Flash Code Details'; Copeland AE8-1328 flash code table

faultCodes.code: Compressor controller ALERT Flash Code 3 - Compressor Protector Trip
faultCodes.meaning: Copeland Digital Compressor Controller ALERT flash code 3: no compressor current is detected when the compressor should be running (demand signal from the system controller is greater than 1.44 VDC and no compressor current is detected). Resets when compressor current is detected. Codes 3, 4, 5 and 9 activate the two-minute anti-short-cycle timer.
likelyCauses: Compressor internal overload / protector open
Contactor not pulled in, open contactor coil circuit (HPS/LPS open), blown fuse, open compressor winding
Current sensor loop not routed through the compressor lead
checks: Check voltage at the contactor load side with a call; verify contactor coil circuit and safeties
Check compressor winding resistance and internal protector (let it cool)
Verify the compressor lead passes through the controller's current sensor
faultCodes.source: AAON RN Series IOM, Table 33 'Compressor Controller ALERT Flash Codes'; Copeland AE8-1328; AAON RN flash code 3 video reference (AE8-1328 R5)

faultCodes.code: Compressor controller ALERT Flash Code 4 - Locked Rotor
faultCodes.meaning: Copeland Digital Compressor Controller ALERT flash code 4: locked rotor condition sensed by the controller on four consecutive start-ups (compressor trips within seconds of each start) within a 20-second window. Activates the two-minute anti-short-cycle timer.
likelyCauses: Seized or mechanically bound scroll
Single-phasing / low voltage on a 3-phase compressor, bad contactor contact
Failed run capacitor (single-phase units)
Liquid slugging on start
checks: Check all three phases at the compressor terminals on a start attempt
Check locked-rotor amps and winding resistance; check for liquid in the crankcase
faultCodes.source: AAON RN Series IOM, Table 33 'Compressor Controller ALERT Flash Codes'; Copeland AE8-1328

faultCodes.code: Compressor controller ALERT Flash Code 5 - Demand Signal Loss
faultCodes.meaning: Copeland Digital Compressor Controller ALERT code for loss of the digital scroll demand signal: demand input signal is below 0.5 VDC; resets after the demand input signal rises above 1.0 VDC. (Code number 5 is taken from the AE8-1328 feature order - High Discharge Temperature, Protector Trip, Locked Rotor, Demand Signal Loss, Discharge Thermistor Fault, Welded Contactor, Low Voltage - confirm on the unit's flash-code label.)
likelyCauses: 0-5 / 1-5 VDC demand wire from the RSMD/VCCX2 open or loose
RSMD analog output failed
Wrong controller configuration for the digital compressor
checks: Measure the demand voltage at the controller's demand terminals with a cooling call
Check the RSMD analog output and wiring
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1328 flash code table (demand signal loss thresholds); AAON RN Series IOM Table 33

faultCodes.code: Compressor controller ALERT Flash Code 6 - Discharge Thermistor Fault
faultCodes.meaning: Copeland Digital Compressor Controller ALERT flash code 6: the controller is not receiving a signal from the discharge temperature thermistor. The thermistor may be missing, disconnected or a wire is broken. The alarm relay contacts will close and the controller will not increase the capacity of the compressor beyond 50 percent loading.
likelyCauses: Discharge thermistor unplugged, broken wire, or open thermistor
Thermistor not installed after compressor replacement
checks: Check thermistor connection and resistance at the controller
Expect capacity limited to 50 percent until repaired (unit will appear low on cooling)
faultCodes.source: AAON RN Series IOM, Table 33 'Compressor Controller ALERT Flash Codes'; Copeland AE8-1328

faultCodes.code: Compressor controller ALERT Flash Code 7 - Unloader Solenoid Fault
faultCodes.meaning: Copeland Digital Compressor Controller ALERT flash code 7: unloader solenoid fault - listed in AE8-1328 as reserved for future use.
likelyCauses: Not normally seen; if displayed, suspect the digital unloader solenoid coil or its wiring
checks: Check the unloader solenoid coil resistance and wiring
faultCodes.source: Copeland AE8-1328 flash code table; AAON RN Series IOM Table 33

faultCodes.code: Compressor controller ALERT Flash Code 8 - Compressor Contactor Fault (Welded Contactor)
faultCodes.meaning: Copeland Digital Compressor Controller ALERT flash code 8: compressor current is detected when the system controller demand signal is below 1.44 VDC. The compressor contactor may have welded contacts.
likelyCauses: Welded / stuck contactor contacts
Contactor coil held in by a wiring fault or BAS override
Current sensor picking up another load
checks: Remove the call and verify the contactor drops out; replace the contactor if contacts are welded
Verify the current sensor loop is on the compressor lead only
faultCodes.source: AAON RN Series IOM, Table 33 'Compressor Controller ALERT Flash Codes'; Copeland AE8-1328

faultCodes.code: Compressor controller ALERT Flash Code 9 - Low Voltage
faultCodes.meaning: Copeland Digital Compressor Controller ALERT flash code 9: low voltage / brown-out condition - the 24 VAC control voltage is too low for reliable operation (all LEDs flashing at the same rate also indicates the 24 VAC supply is too low for operation). Activates the two-minute anti-short-cycle timer.
likelyCauses: Overloaded or undersized control transformer
High resistance in the 24 VAC circuit, poor common connection
Low line voltage
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the controller under load; check transformer VA and line voltage
faultCodes.source: AAON RN Series IOM, Table 33 'Compressor Controller ALERT Flash Codes'; Copeland AE8-1328

ledPatterns.meaning: An alarm is present; the specific alarm is displayed on the LCD / System Manager
checks: Read the alarm text on the LCD or via the System Manager TS-L / TS II

ledPatterns.pattern: POWER, APP HB, OS HB, WDOG, STATUS 1/2, EBUS, LOOP COMM, BACNET, RLY1–RLY8 LEDs
ledPatterns.meaning: Power, application and OS heartbeats, watchdog, status, E-BUS, loop communication, BACnet activity and relay output states — used for diagnostics
checks: A steady heartbeat LED that stops blinking indicates a halted controller — cycle power
RLY LEDs show which outputs (fan, cooling/heating stages) are commanded

ledPatterns.meaning: A diagnostic LED that lights up and stays lit when there is an alarm present; the specific alarm text is on the LCD alarm screen, the System Manager TS II, Prism 2, or BACnet.
checks: Scroll the LCD 'Alarms' screen (press ENTER to step through, or let it auto-scroll) to read the alarm names

ledPatterns.pattern: VCCX2 STATUS 2 LED blinks once every 10 seconds
checks: No action

ledPatterns.pattern: VCCX2 STATUS 2 LED blinks twice every 10 seconds
ledPatterns.meaning: An override is active (a point is being overridden from the service tool, System Manager, or BAS).
checks: Find and release the override in Prism 2 / service tool or the BACnet priority array before diagnosing 'wrong' operation

ledPatterns.pattern: VCCX2 STATUS 2 LED blinks three times every 10 seconds
ledPatterns.meaning: One of the outputs is in Force mode.
checks: Release forced outputs in the service tool when testing is complete

ledPatterns.meaning: Diagnostic blink-code LED that should not be blinking under normal operation; blinking indicates a controller problem.
checks: Cycle controller power; if it persists, contact AAON Controls support with the blink count

ledPatterns.pattern: VCCX2 POWER, APP HB, OS HB, WDOG, EBUS, LOOP COMM, BACNET, RLY1-RLY8 LEDs
ledPatterns.meaning: Power applied; application and operating-system heartbeats (should blink continuously); watchdog; E-BUS activity to expansion modules; local loop communication; BACnet activity; and the commanded state of each relay output.
checks: A heartbeat LED that stops blinking indicates a halted controller - cycle power
RLY LEDs show which outputs (fan, cooling/heating stages) are commanded; compare with what is actually running

ledPatterns.pattern: VCC-X EM1 expansion module ALARM LED on, relays off, analog outputs at 0 VDC
ledPatterns.meaning: The EM1 module has not received communications from the VCCX2 for more than 1 minute (loss of E-BUS communication).
checks: Check the E-BUS cable between the VCCX2 and the EM1; the EM1 COMM LED should blink on and off every time it receives a valid E-BUS request

ledPatterns.pattern: RSMD / RSMD-CM / RM454 ALARM LED above the LCD lit red and blinking
ledPatterns.meaning: An alarm is present on the refrigerant system module; the alarms display and scroll automatically from the module's ALARMS screen ('NO ALARMS' when none).
checks: Read the module's ALARMS screen; low-suction, high-head and compressor lockouts on the RSMD require cycling power to the module to clear

ledPatterns.pattern: AAON Compressor Protection Module (G143890) status LED steady green
ledPatterns.meaning: Unit is powered up and the module is not detecting any fault conditions.
checks: No action

ledPatterns.pattern: AAON Compressor Protection Module (G143890) status LED flashing red, N flashes
ledPatterns.meaning: The module has detected a fault condition and is now in alarm mode; the number of flashes indicates what alarm is present (see 'Alarm Status LED Diagnostic Codes' in the CPM technical guide - the per-count table was not captured).
checks: Count the flashes and look them up in the CPM technical guide G143890 'Alarm Status LED Diagnostic Codes' table

ledPatterns.pattern: Compressor controller (Copeland Digital Compressor Controller) TRIP LED on
ledPatterns.meaning: The compressor protector is open, or supply power to the compressor is missing.
checks: Check voltage to the compressor and the internal protector; let the compressor cool

ledPatterns.meaning: The anti-short-cycle timer is active (2 minutes after codes 3, 4, 5, 9; 30 minutes after code 2).
checks: Wait out the timer; do not cycle power repeatedly to bypass it

ledPatterns.pattern: Compressor controller ALERT LED flashes N times, pauses, repeats
ledPatterns.meaning: The number of consecutive flashes is the Flash Code and correlates to a particular abnormal condition: 2 High Discharge Temperature, 3 Compressor Protector Trip, 4 Locked Rotor, 5 Demand Signal Loss, 6 Discharge Thermistor Fault, 7 Unloader Solenoid Fault (reserved), 8 Compressor Contactor Fault (welded contactor), 9 Low Voltage; code 1 reserved for future use.
checks: See the matching 'Compressor controller ALERT Flash Code N' fault entries

ledPatterns.pattern: Compressor controller: all LEDs flashing at the same rate
ledPatterns.meaning: 24 VAC supply is too low for operation.
checks: Measure 24 VAC at the controller; check the transformer and connections

diagnosticTips: The controller LCD and LEDs are on the VCCX2 board in the unit control compartment; the System Manager TS-L / TS II (wall or unit mounted) shows status, alarms and setpoints.
The Low Suction Pressure alarm is a hard lockout: fix the cause, then cycle controller power to clear.
Many AAON compressor and refrigerant faults are detected by the RSMD/CPM modules and then reported by the VCCX2 — check those modules' own LEDs (CPM technical guide G143890, RSMD guide G039810).
Controls support: AAON Controls (918) 382-6450 / support.controls@aaon.com.

Where to look: the VCCX2 board (LEDs and 2-line LCD with keypad) is in the unit's control compartment; the System Manager TS II or the LCD alarm screen shows 'No Alarms' or 'Alarms' - press ENTER to scroll through the active alarms or let them auto-scroll. Prism 2 (PC software) and the Modular Service Tool show the same alarms with full names, and alarms must be configured in Prism 2 to be reported.

The VCCX2 detects sensor open/short by input voltage: above 4.88 VDC = open sensor or wiring, below 0.05 VDC = short. For Space, Supply, Outdoor or Return temperature sensors you can check resistance with the sensor disconnected or voltage while connected. RSMD transducer inputs use 4.98 VDC (open) / 0.38 VDC (short).

Refrigerant-side faults (low suction, high head, compressor fault, transducer failure) are detected by the RSMD / RSMD2R / RSMD-CM / RM454 refrigerant system module and passed to the VCCX2 over E-BUS - read the module's own ALARMS screen and diagnostic (pressure) screens. Low Suction, High Head and 5-in-4-hour compressor lockouts require cycling power to the module to clear.

AAON RN/RQ digital-scroll units have a Copeland Digital Compressor Controller per digital compressor: read the ALERT LED flash count and TRIP LED (RN IOM 'Compressor Controller Flash Code Details'). Newer units may use the AAON Compressor Protection Module (G143890) whose status LED is green (OK) or flashing red with a flash count.
If configured, the VCCX2 Alarm Active relay energizes any time a VCCX2 alarm is active - useful for a BAS binary alarm point.

STATUS 2 LED blinking 2x or 3x every 10 s means an override or forced output is active - release overrides (service tool, System Manager, or BACnet priority array) before troubleshooting unexpected operation.
The optional AAON Touchscreen Controller (obsolete) lists alarms under 'General Alarms' (p.61) and 'Shutdown Alarms' (p.62) of its user manual; its alarm names were not captured here.
Controls support: AAON Controls (918) 382-6450 / support.controls@aaon.com; VCCX2 technical guide G039840 (ASM01698), RSMD guide G039810, RSMD2R G088350, CPM G143890.

components.notes: LED flash codes; Modbus link to the RTU-C on RKNL-C+

components.name: Indoor blower motor (belt drive or ECM depending on size)
Main limit switch / roll-out switch (gas units)

safetyDevices: Freeze protection via economizer/low-ambient controls where fitted
sequenceOfOperation: Cooling (thermostat/RTU-C): Y1 + G → indoor blower energized (G, or after the controller's fan delay); with HPS/LPS closed the controller closes CC for compressor 1 and starts the condenser fan; Y2 adds compressor 2 / second stage. With a JADE economizer and suitable outdoor air, the economizer satisfies first-stage cooling with the dampers before mechanical cooling is staged.

Gas heating: W1 → IFC starts the inducer (IDM), proves the pressure switch (PS), runs pre-purge, energizes the hot-surface igniter and gas valve (GV), proves flame at FS, then starts the indoor blower after the heat-on delay; W2 drives high fire on two-stage units. Limit (LS) or roll-out (RO) opening shuts the gas valve and produces a 3-flash code.
Electric heat (RL units): W1/W2 energize heater contactors through the limit string with the blower running.
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE — designators are common Rheem wiring-diagram usage from builder recollection, NOT transcribed from a specific IOM legend. Read the legend on the wiring diagram glued inside the control-box cover; the same diagram is in the IOM (92-23577-80 series for RKNL-B/C).

sequenceOfOperation: Cooling: on a space/supply-air demand the VCCX2 proves the supply fan (fan proving input), then stages cooling — the digital scroll (VCC) modulates 10–100 % as first stage, fixed compressors add capacity; condenser fan speed is modulated by the head-pressure module for head-pressure control. Economizer dampers modulate first when outdoor conditions allow.

Heating: the VCCX2 stages gas or electric heat through its relay outputs (or modulates a gas valve) to hold the supply-air setpoint; the gas heat section's own ignition control handles ignition and limits.
Low suction pressure below setpoint for 1 minute (or < 40 psi for 5 s) shuts the system down; power must be cycled to clear.
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE — component list is builder recollection plus the AAON technical training guides and controls literature named below, not a transcribed wiring-diagram legend. Every AAON unit ships with order-specific wiring diagrams in the control compartment — use those.
Digital scroll modulation (VCC) means measured superheat/subcooling swing with loading — force 100 % capacity via the controller before evaluating charge.

commonIssues.symptom: Gas heat locks out with 2 flashes on the IFC (pressure switch open) — often after rain or during cooling season changeover
likelyCauses: Condensate line clogged, backing water into the pressure-switch hose
Blocked vent/flue or combustion-air inlet (nests, debris)
Weak inducer
checks: Pull the pressure-switch hose and check for water; clear the drain/trap
Measure draft at the switch with the inducer running
Inspect the vent hood and flue

commonIssues.symptom: Renaissance unit (RKNL-C+) shows A15 and will not run
likelyCauses: RTU-C controller fault
Control-power quality problem
checks: Cycle power; verify 24 VAC control power under load
Replace the RTU-C if A15 returns
sources: justanswer thread: A15 controller fault on Rheem commercial unit

commonIssues.symptom: Economizer not economizing / JADE shows a sensor error; unit runs mechanical cooling in mild weather
likelyCauses: Failed or disconnected OA/MA sensor (MAT SENS ERR, OA SYLK T/H ERR)
Actuator undervoltage (ACT UNDER V) from a loaded 24 VAC transformer
Damper linkage or actuator failure
checks: Read the ALARMS menu on the JADE
Check sensor wiring/resistance; measure 24 VAC at the actuator
Use CHECKOUT to stroke the damper

commonIssues.symptom: AAON unit trips on Low Suction Pressure and locks out until power is cycled
likelyCauses: Low charge/leak
Low airflow (filters, fan VFD speed, iced coil)
Restricted metering device
Suction transducer/wiring fault
checks: Compare transducer to gauge
Force compressor to 100 % via the controller before charge evaluation
Check filters, VFD speed command and coil
sources: VCCX2 Controller Technical Guide G039840 (alarm description)

commonIssues.symptom: AAON digital scroll (VCC) unit: erratic superheat/subcooling readings, apparent under/overcharge
likelyCauses: Digital scroll unloading (10–100 % modulation) during the reading — pressures swing with the loading cycle
Genuine charge problem masked by modulation
checks: Force the VCC to 100 % from the controller and let pressures stabilize before reading
Charge to the nameplate subcooling with the compressor at full capacity
Check the RSMD/CPM status LEDs for compressor faults
sources: AAON Rooftop Unit Technical Training Guide (Total HVAC Inc.) describing VCC modulation; charging-at-100 % practice from builder recollection

commonIssues.symptom: AAON unit: high head pressure / condenser fan not modulating
likelyCauses: Head-pressure control module or EC condenser fan motor failure
Condenser fan VFD fault or min/max frequency mis-set
Dirty condenser coil
checks: Verify the 0–10 V signal from the head-pressure module to the EC motor/VFD
Check VFD fault log and programmed min/max frequencies
Clean the coil
sources: AAON Rooftop Unit Technical Training Guide (Total HVAC Inc.): head-pressure module paired with EC motor or VFD

commonIssues.symptom: AAON unit: economizer damper stuck / excess outdoor air, poor temperature control and high energy use
likelyCauses: Economizer damper or actuator failure
Poor economizer control setup (sensors, changeover setpoints)
Blocked/binding damper blades
checks: Command the damper via the controller and watch the actuator
Verify OA/RA sensor readings and economizer setpoints in the VCCX2
Inspect blades/linkage for obstruction

commonIssues.symptom: AAON unit: vibration and rattling noises
likelyCauses: Loose panels or screws
Fan wheel / belt / bearing wear
Compressor mounting
checks: Tighten panels and hardware
Inspect blower bearings, belts and wheel balance
